title: Hospitality + Tourism Cluster Exam
blurb: Practice questions reused from two openly licensed textbooks: an open BC tourism and hospitality textbook (tourism, events, risk, law, safety) and an open customer-service textbook (handling upset customers, goal setting).
disclaimer: Questions reused from openly licensed sources (credited on each question). Not official DECA exam content.
coverageNote: Built only from non-OpenStax sources mapped in SOURCES.md 5.5; 81 OpenStax items stay in _hold-openstax/exams/hospitality-tourism.json until OpenStax grants permission. This is a short practice set, not a full 100-item exam, and it does not follow the blueprint mix. Areas with no item here: Information Management (blueprint 14/15/15), Financial Analysis, Selling, Economics, Communications, Strategic Management, Human Resources Management, Marketing, Pricing, Quality Management and Knowledge Management. Operations has 1 item (workplace safety), with no lodging or food-service items. Customer Relations items come from a customer-contact-centre context. Several BC items are Canada- or BC-specific (WorkSafeBC, TIAC, Destination Canada, Canadian tort law). Difficulty was estimated by reading each item. Choices keep the source order, and H5P Single Choice Sets always list the key first, so keys are uneven: A 9, B 0, C 6, D 4. No item has an "all/none of the above" option, so the app can shuffle choices safely. Verification on 2026-10-11 removed 5 items (see verification.notes), leaving 19.

notes: Method: each of the 24 items was solved before its key was read. On 2026-10-11 the verifier fetched every cited chapter page (8 BC, 2 Customer Centric Strategy) and the H5P data for every cited activity through each book’s h5p_embed endpoint (BC ids 6, 19, 25, 39, 40, 41, 42, 44, 54; CCS ids 3, 5). Stems, choices and keys were compared word for word, and the licence statement was confirmed on every cited page: BC CC BY 4.0 and CCS CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, both "except where otherwise noted". The BC home page’s required attribution ("...by Wendy Anderson and Morgan Westcott (Editors) is used under a CC BY 4.0 Licence. Download for free from the B.C. Open Collection.") matches the attribution lines.

All 24 items matched their H5P source word for word, typos included, and every key matched the H5P correct flag or the SingleChoiceSet first answer. Activity titles and H5P authors in the attribution lines match the H5P metadata. The trims on ht-029, ht-064, ht-065 and ht-090 removed only options the source marks wrong: "Figure out who to blame", "Historic sites", "Destination marketing organizations (DMO)" (section 7.1 lists DMOs), and Germany and Mexico.

Removed ht-097 (carbon offsetting) as ambiguous. A and B differ only in "standardized, regulated" versus "unregulated". The book’s own glossary defines carbon offsetting as "A market-based system that provides options for organizations to invest in green initiatives to offset their own carbon emissions", with no claim of regulation, and voluntary offset markets are widely described as unregulated. B is therefore defensible, and the source cannot fix the key.

Removed ht-103, ht-104, ht-105 and ht-106 (CCS Chapter 4 quiz) on licence grounds. The build flag "Nothing from the video or its transcript is used here" was wrong. The quiz follows the Userlike video "How to Deal With Angry Customers", which is all rights reserved (transcript: https://ecampusontario.pressbooks.pub/app/uploads/sites/3453/2023/07/How-to-Deal-with-Angry-Customers-Transcript.pdf). These four items turn transcript sentences into the stem and key. ht-103: "dealing with angry customers on a regular basis is tough on your well-being. It can even lead to burnout." ht-104: "It will only make them feel like you're not understanding their view or taking them seriously." ht-105: "calming the customer down should be your first priority. Focus on handling the person first and then the issue." ht-106 reuses the washing-machine phone example and "I'm sorry your phone stopped working. I understand that this is very frustrating for you. This lets you apologize for the situation and show compassion but not take any of the blame." The book does not credit this wording to the video, so the expression traces to an all-rights-reserved source, not to the CC BY-NC-SA book.

Kept CCS items checked against the same transcript: ht-098, ht-099, ht-100, ht-101 and ht-102 cover the same topics but in wording that does not appear in it. ht-107 was checked against the transcript of the Chapter 3 SMART-goals video (21-SMART-Goals-Transcript.pdf), and its goal examples do not appear there.
Fixed 1: in ht-107’s explanation, the Table 3.1 cell reads "Make your goals specific and narrow for more effective planning" with no full stop, so the period now sits outside the quote.

Kept after a close look. ht-099: active listening can also calm a customer, but paraphrasing exists to check understanding, so C is the single best answer (source key). ht-082: D, "Transfers the acceptance of negligence", is a distractor, since section 11.3 states the purpose as "transfers acceptance of the risk". ht-063: the book defines a tourist as staying at least 24 hours and an excursionist as a same-day visitor, so D is the only fit. ht-065: section 7.1’s list names travel agencies, OTAs, tour operators and DMOs, while GDS appears later in 7.1 as a booking tool, so only C fits. App users cannot see the book list, so the explanation carries that context. ht-016: go2HR does safety promotion but not rehabilitation or wage compensation, so only WorkSafeBC fits all three clauses.
